- [FACT] User is planning a family tree project to preserve family history and memories.
- [TEMPORAL] User's 40th birthday was in April.
- [PREFERENCE] User is thinking about their own mortality a lot lately.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Creating a family tree project is a great way to preserve family history and memories and leave a lasting legacy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended online tools and resources for building a family tree: 
  1. Ancestry.com (subscription-based)
  2. FamilySearch.org (free)
  3. MyHeritage (subscription-based)
  4. Findmypast (subscription-based)
  5. Legacy Family Tree (one-time purchase or subscription)
  6. FamilyTreeMaker (one-time purchase or subscription)
  7. WikiTree (free)
  8. Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel (for simple family trees)
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested additional resources: 
  - Local libraries and archives for genealogy databases and expert assistance.
  - Family history centers operated by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
  - DNA testing services from companies like AncestryDNA, 23andMe, and FamilyTreeDNA.
  - Scanning and digitization tools for old family photos and documents.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised user to gather information from living relatives, organize existing family documents, and set clear goals for the project.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Building a family tree is a journey, and it's okay to start small.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It's normal to think about mortality around milestone birthdays, and creating a family tree can be a meaningful way to leave a legacy.
